extracted.intended_audience: researchers, program officers, and policymakers studying grant peer review processes (e.g., NIH study sections), and scholars interested in peer review reliability and discourse
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and measurement criteria for studying scoring behavior, reliability, and interactional discourse (Score Calibration Talk) in NIH-like grant peer review panels; includes operational definitions, quantitative metrics, and coding rules used to evaluate meetings and score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krippendorff's α reliability thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: A value of α ≥ 0.8 is considered ‘reliable’, and values between 0.67 and 0.8 are considered suitable for drawing ‘tentative conclusions’ (Krippendorff 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Krippendorff’s α to quantify interrater/inter-panel agreement. Interpret α≥0.8 as reliable, 0.67–0.8 as tentative; lower values indicate low reliability and caution in inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion for score analyses (discussed applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: These analyses only included those applications that were discussed in a meeting (i.e. the top scoring 50%) because those are the only applications that receive final scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing preliminary vs final scores or computing final-score reliability, restrict to discussed applications (top ~50%) because nondiscussed applications do not have final scores; report when analyses use only discussed subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score types (preliminary, final reviewer, final panel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between Preliminary Reviewer Scores (individual reviewers' pre-meeting scores), Final Reviewer Scores (individual reviewers' scores after discussion), and Final Panel Scores (the panel's average/final score for an application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit which score type an analysis references; comparisons (e.g., within- vs between-panel) should define whether they use reviewer-level averages or panel-level averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Within-panel agreement (measure and expected direction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement among reviewers within a panel substantially improves after collaborative discussion for both the Final Reviewer Scores and the Final Panel Scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure within-panel agreement via paired-samples t-tests on ranges and Krippendorff’s α; expect decrease in within-panel score range (score convergence) after discussion; report effect sizes, SDs, and p-values, and caution about sample size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Between-panel agreement (measure and observed pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the spread among panels of Preliminary Reviewer Scores for a given application with the spread among panels of the Final Reviewer Scores for that same application; in this study, between-panel variability increased after discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize between-panel variability as the range of panel-average scores across panels for the same application and quantify with range comparisons and Krippendorff’s α; do not assume panel discussion reduces between-panel variability—report both range and α.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Score Calibration Talk (SCT) (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: SCT: instances of discourse in which reviewers make explicit references to the scoring habits of fellow panelists; a genre of talk that establishes common ground about the meaning of numeric scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat SCT as a measurable discourse phenomenon that may relate to score changes and convergence; define and code SCT occurrences systematically in transcripts/videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-initiated Score Calibration Talk (S-SCT) — operational definition
rubrics_metrics.description: S-SCT is any instance of discourse during which reviewers mention their scores (either the word ‘score’ or the number itself) along with an account (i.e. the rationale or justification) for that score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code as S-SCT only when the speaker provides an account or rationale (e.g., 'The reason I gave it a four was mainly due to problems with the approach'). A bare announcement like 'I gave it a four' is NOT S-SCT. S-SCT can ground a reviewer’s interpretation of what numerical scores mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other-initiated Score Calibration Talk (O-SCT) — operational definition
rubrics_metrics.description: O-SCT is any instance of discourse during which one panelist calls on other reviewers to account for their scoring practices by offering a ‘challenge’ to their score (e.g., known-answer questions that function as challenges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code as O-SCT when a speaker challenges another's score (e.g., 'You gave it a score of one, right?' posed to elicit account). Do not code routine information-seeking (e.g., 'What was your score again?') as O-SCT unless it functions as a challenge or is followed by a challenge. O-SCT episodes can be brief or span multiple speakers and turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCT episode boundaries and coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An instance of SCT begins with the initiation of S-SCT or O-SCT and ends when the participants move to a new project (e.g., a chair opens the floor for new comments); specific start/end markers are used in coding (see Supplementary Appendix B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear start and end markers for episodes when coding SCT (e.g., an O-SCT episode continues until the Vice-chairperson begins a new project). Document how cross-application re-invocations are handled (SCT can span applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: SCT counts and duration as quantitative metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Count the number of instances of S-SCT, O-SCT, and Total SCT and measure the total time spent on each (reported as minutes:seconds per CSS and total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both raw counts and cumulative time (e.g., Table 4 reports numbers and m:s). Use counts and time as separate but related measures; account for rare events (small counts) when interpreting correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between SCT (count/time) and score changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute correlations between number/time of SCT instances and number/percentage of times reviewers changed their scores. In this study: Total SCT correlated with score change (r = 0.717), S-SCT weakly (r = 0.107), O-SCT strongly (r = 0.978); time-based correlations show similar patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both raw counts and time spent as predictors; interpret correlations cautiously with small n and non-independence. Expect O-SCT to be more strongly associated with score changes than S-SCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score convergence metric within panels (range_final − range_prelim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the difference between the range in Preliminary Reviewer Scores and the range in Final Reviewer Scores within each panel (range_final − range_prelim) as a measure of within-panel convergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive decreases in range indicate convergence. Correlate this difference with SCT counts/time to test whether SCT relates to convergence (study found strong positive relationships for Total SCT and O-SCT, weaker/variable for S-SCT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Score divergence metric between panels (range PanelFinal − range PanelPrelim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute change in the range of average scores between panels for the same application (rangePanelFinal − rangePanelPrelim) to assess between-panel divergence after discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both within-panel convergence and between-panel divergence; the study found that greater within-panel convergence tended to be associated with greater between-panel divergence (correlation r = −0.606 for the relationship between differences in ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of paired-samples t-tests and significance thresholds for small samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Paired-samples t-tests were used to compare ranges/pre-post measures; with small n, significance was considered at α = 0.10 in some tests (e.g., t11 = −2.185, p = 0.051 reported for n = 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sample sizes are small, consider and report the α level used, effect sizes, and caution about power. Avoid overinterpreting marginal p-values and report exact statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final score reporting sequence (procedural anchor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the final score reporting sequence (Raclaw and Ford 2015) in which reviewers announce final scores and panelists privately cast their scores; this sequence provides moments for SCT to occur and be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the formal score-reporting sequence as a structured point for coding score announcements and associated SCT; note when reviewers change scores during or immediately after this sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting SCT influence cautiously (sample, dependence, and coding limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of small sample sizes, low per-application SCT counts, lack of independence across discussions, and some panels having zero or one O-SCT per application, correlations should be interpreted cautiously and causal claims avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report limitations: few panels/applications/reviewers, constructed study sections (ecological validity concerns), voluntary sampling bias toward higher-scoring applications. Avoid causal language and specify these constraints when generalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical interventions to reduce variability (recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential interventions include using a jigsaw technique (mixing reviewers across groups) to allow 'osmosis' of SCT and score norming, or providing ‘standard’ benchmark applications that all study sections evaluate to calibrate scoring practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing interventions, align them with observed mechanisms (e.g., O-SCT driving convergence) and design experimental tests to evaluate effects on within- and between-panel reliability.
